bug_description.original: The fuzzer contains an off by one error, passing an incorrect length to the CharReader::parse method in a way that results in a heap buffer overflow.
bug_description.normalized: The staged vulnerable harness in `src/test_lib_json/fuzz.cpp` reads a 4-byte settings header from the exact 10-byte witness `f3 a0 80 aa 38 2f 2a 36 27 00`, advances `data` by 4 bytes, but never subtracts those 4 bytes from `size`. It then calls `reader->parse(data_str, data_str + size, ...)`, where `data_str` points at the remaining 6-byte payload `8/*6'\0` but `endDoc` is still computed 10 bytes ahead, four bytes past the real testcase allocation. `Json::OurReader::parse` stores that overstated `[begin_, end_)` span, `readValue()` parses the leading `8`, and the post-value scan tokenizes the remaining `/*6'\0` bytes as a C-style comment. `readCStyleComment()` uses the stale `end_` bound, so once `current_` reaches the true end of the 10-byte libFuzzer buffer, `getNextChar()` still treats one more byte as in-range and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow read at `json_reader.cpp:1791`.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the malformed parser span and materializes it into reader state. It stores the shifted payload pointer as `begin_`, the stale end pointer as `end_`, and initializes `current_` at the payload start.
source.value_from: The harness advances `data` by 4 bytes and then calls `reader->parse(data_str, data_str + size, ...)` with the original `size == 10`. For the exact witness `f3 a0 80 aa 38 2f 2a 36 27 00`, `beginDoc` therefore points at the 6-byte suffix `8/*6'\0` while `endDoc` is four bytes past the real allocation.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `getNextChar()` dereferences `current_` after comment scanning has already advanced it to the first byte past the 10-byte testcase buffer, so the read happens just beyond the heap allocation that libFuzzer created for the witness.
sink.note: The staged sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` in `getNextChar /src/jsoncpp/src/lib_json/json_reader.cpp:1791:10`, and says the faulting address is 0 bytes to the right of the 10-byte region `[0x6020000000b0, 0x6020000000ba)`.

root_cause.description: The harness skips the 4-byte settings header by advancing `data`, but it leaves `size` unchanged. The remaining payload is therefore shorter than the length later used to derive the parser end pointer.
root_cause.note: The fix adds the missing paired update `size -= sizeof(uint32_t);` immediately after this statement, keeping the shifted pointer and remaining length consistent before the later `reader->parse(...)` call.

parser_admitted.description: For the exact post-header payload `8/*6'\0`, `readValue()` succeeds by parsing the leading `8` as a number and returns with `current_` positioned at the following `/`, so the parser reaches the post-value `skipCommentTokens(token)` scan at line 1048 instead of failing earlier.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant state is the stale remaining length. After the 4-byte header skip, only 6 in-allocation bytes remain, but `size` still holds the original total 10 and later becomes the `+ size` used to derive `endDoc`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Exact witness bytes `f3 a0 80 aa 38 2f 2a 36 27 00`; after the skip the parser-visible payload is `38 2f 2a 36 27 00` (`8/*6'\0`).

coarse_trace.summary: The harness strips the 4-byte settings header from the 10-byte witness but keeps the original `size`, then calls `reader->parse` with a begin/end pair that extends four bytes past the real payload.
The parser stores the overstated span in `begin_/end_/current_` and parses the leading `8`, leaving `current_` at the slash that starts the trailing `/*6'\0` bytes.
The post-value scan treats the remaining bytes as a comment token, and `readComment()` selects the C-style comment path because the byte after `/` is `*`.

The C-style comment scanner uses the stale `end_` bound, continues after `current_` reaches the true end of the testcase buffer, and `getNextChar()` performs the 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read reported by ASan.

fine_trace.note: This skips the 4-byte settings header at the front of the 10-byte witness, leaving only the six-byte payload `38 2f 2a 36 27 00` in-bounds. `size` is not reduced here, so it still represents the original 10-byte testcase allocation.

fine_trace.code:
const char* data_str = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(data);
  reader->parse(data_str, data_str + size, &root, nullptr);
fine_trace.note: The harness casts the shifted payload pointer to `data_str` and computes `endDoc = data_str + size`. Because step 1 left `size == 10` while only 6 bytes remain after `data`, the call passes a parser span that extends four bytes past the testcase buffer.

Source. The first non-harness parser state assignment stores the malformed span from step 2. For the exact witness this makes `begin_` point at `8/*6'\0`, `current_ = begin_`, and `end_` point four bytes past the real buffer end.

`readValue()` consumes the leading `8` as a number token. `readNumber(false)` stops when it encounters `/`, so `successful` is true and `current_` is left on the slash that begins the remaining tail `/*6'\0`.

The post-value `skipCommentTokens(token)` call at line 1048 now tokenizes the remaining slash byte. `readToken()` classifies it as `tokenComment` and dispatches into `readComment()` instead of reaching end-of-stream.
`readComment()` consumes the byte after `/`. For the witness that byte is `*`, so the parser takes the C-style comment branch and starts scanning for a closing `*/` using the overstated `end_` bound.

This loop trusts `end_` from step 3 as the comment extent. After it consumes the in-bounds bytes `6`, `'`, and `\0`, `current_` reaches the actual end of the 10-byte testcase, but `(current_ + 1) < end_` is still true because `end_` was set four bytes too far.

Sink. On the next loop iteration from step 7, `getNextChar()` executes with `current_` already equal to the first byte past the 10-byte libFuzzer allocation, so dereferencing `*current_` produces the 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read that ASan reports at address `0x6020000000ba`.

crash_stack.function: Json::OurReader::parse(char const*, char const*, Json::Value&, bool)
Json::OurCharReader::parse(char const*, char const*, Json::Value*, std::__1::basic_string<char, std::__1::char_traits<char>, std::__1::allocator<char> >*)

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch adds `size -= sizeof(uint32_t);` immediately after the header skip, so the later parse call uses the true 6-byte remaining extent instead of the original 10-byte total size.

format.name: 10-byte jsoncpp fuzzer witness
format.contract: Exact 10-byte input `f3 a0 80 aa 38 2f 2a 36 27 00`: the first 4 bytes are consumed as the fuzz settings header, then the remaining 6-byte payload `8/*6'\0` is parsed with the original total `size` still equal to 10, causing `reader->parse` to receive an end pointer four bytes past the real payload.
